pr_title: refactor: use traditional parameters where possible
pr_body:

### Description of change

<!--
  Please be clear and concise what the change is intended to do,
  why this change is needed, and how you've verified that it
  corrects what you intended.

  In some cases it may be helpful to include the current behavior
  and the new behavior.

  If the change is related to an open issue, you can link it here.
  If you include `Fixes #0000` (replacing `0000` with the issue number)
  when this is merged it will automatically mark the issue as fixed and
  close it.
-->

fixes #7111
fixes #4429

this refactors a wide variety of use-cases for parameters.

* drops the native parameters out of use but leaves them in place for compatibility purposes
* refactors the parameter replacement to improve performance drastically
* allows for nested querybuilders without parameter overwriting (such as with `Brackets`
* aligns the escape parameters functions across drivers

It's a public API and could be used by third parties.

Back of the napkin, no negligible difference.  Timing was incredibly hard to see a difference over 10m inserts in batches of 100 & 10,000

This might resolve some of the issues in #3857

issue_context.title: Postgres query with a large amount of entities fails because of regexp
issue_context.body:
## Issue Description
Can't execute a query with a lot of entities (checked with ~120,000 entities) using Postgres.

### Expected Behavior
The query succeeds and the entities are retuned.

### Actual Behavior
The query fails and throws the following error:

```
Invalid regular expression: ... : Too many captures
at new Regexp(<anonymous>)
at PostgresDriver.escapeQueryWithParameters(.../PostgresDriver.ts(566:27))
```

### My Environment
| Dependency          | Version  |
| ---                 | ---      |
| Operating System    |     Windows 10     |
| Node.js version     | v13.9.0 |
| Typescript version  | v3.9.5 |
| TypeORM version     | v0.2.22 |

### Relevant Database Driver(s)
- [ ] `aurora-data-api`
- [ ] `aurora-data-api-pg`
- [ ] `better-sqlite3`
- [ ] `cockroachdb`
- [ ] `cordova`
- [ ] `expo`
- [ ] `mongodb`
- [ ] `mysql`
- [ ] `nativescript`
- [ ] `oracle`
- [X] `postgres`
- [ ] `react-native`
- [ ] `sap`
- [ ] `sqlite`
- [ ] `sqlite-abstract`
- [ ] `sqljs`
- [ ] `sqlserver`

### Are you willing to resolve this issue by submitting a Pull Request?
- [ ] Yes, I have the time, and I know how to start.
- [ ] Yes, I have the time, but I don't know how to start. I would need guidance.
- [ ] No, I don't have the time, although I believe I could do it if I had the time...
- [X] No, I don't have the time and I wouldn't even know how to start.
comments: Have you considered performing the insert as part of multiple queries in blocks of e.g. 1000 entities, perhaps inside of a transaction? If the RegExp didn't fail you may well have encountered other issues, so such large inserts are probably best avoided.

Thanks for the quick reply.
I'm trying to fetch the entities, not insert them.

Any updates on this issue?
Did you find a way around @ronkatz96 ?

I use version: 0.2.31 and had the same issue with hundreds of parameters.

```
SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: /(:(\\\\.\\\\.\\\\.)?slotId0\\\\b)|(:(\\\\.\\\\.\\\\.)?slotId1\\\\b)|... (Too many captures)
at String.replace (<anonymous>),
at PostgresDriver.escapeQueryWithParameters (src/driver/postgres/PostgresDriver.ts:617:19),
```
